<laravel-boost-guidelines>
Laravel Boost guidelines for this Laravel app must be followed to ensure best experience. This project is Laravel app with packages/versions: inertiajs/inertia-laravel (INERTIA) v2; laravel/fortify (FORTIFY) v1; laravel/framework (LARAVEL) v12; laravel/prompts (PROMPTS) v0; laravel/wayfinder (WAYFINDER) v0; laravel/boost (BOOST) v2; laravel/mcp (MCP) v0; laravel/pail (PAIL) v1; laravel/pint (PINT) v1; laravel/sail (SAIL) v1; pestphp/pest (PEST) v4; phpunit/phpunit (PHPUNIT) v12. Activate relevant skill whenever in that domain: `wayfinder-development` (when referencing backend routes in frontend components; use when importing from @/actions or @/routes, calling Laravel routes from TypeScript, or working with Wayfinder route functions). `pest-testing` (Tests with Pest 4; writing tests, unit/feature, assertions, testing Livewire components, browser testing, debugging test failures, datasets/mocking; or when user mentions test/spec/TDD/expect/coverage/needs to verify functionality). Follow existing code conventions; when creating/editing file, check sibling files for correct structure/approach/naming. Use descriptive variable/method names (e.g., `isRegisteredForDiscounts`). Check for existing components to reuse. Do not create verification scripts or tinker when tests cover that functionality and prove they work; unit/feature tests are more important. Stick to existing directory structure; don't create new base folders without approval. Do not change app dependencies without approval. If no frontend change reflected, ask to run `npm run build`, `npm run dev`, or `composer run dev`. Only create documentation files if explicitly requested. Be concise. Use Laravel Boost MCP tools. Use `list-artisan-commands` to double-check Artisan command parameters. Whenever sharing a project URL, use `get-absolute-url` to ensure correct scheme/domain/IP/port. Must use `tinker` to execute PHP to debug code or query Eloquent models directly. Use `database-query` to only read database. Use `database-schema` to inspect table structure before migrations/models. Use `browser-logs` (Boost) to read browser logs/errors/exceptions; only recent logs. Use `search-docs` before other approaches for Laravel/Laravel ecosystem; it passes installed packages/versions and returns version-specific docs. Pass package filters array if needed. Always use version-specific docs with `search-docs` for Inertia, Laravel, Pest, etc. Use multiple broad simple topic-based queries at once; example: `['rate limiting', 'routing rate limiting', 'routing']`. Do not add package names to queries; package info already shared. Query patterns for search-docs: 1) Simple Word Searches with auto-stemming - query=authentication finds 'authenticate' and 'auth'. 2) Multiple Words (AND Logic) - query=rate limit finds both "rate" AND "limit". 3) Quoted Phrases (Exact Position) - query="infinite scroll" words adjacent/order. 4) Mixed Queries - query=middleware "rate limit" middleware AND exact phrase. 5) Multiple Queries - queries=["authentication","middleware"] ANY of these terms.
Control structures: always use curly braces even for single-line bodies. In PHP constructors use property promotion in `__construct()`:
`public function __construct(public GitHub $github) { }`
Do not allow empty `__construct()` with zero parameters unless constructor is private. Always use explicit return type declarations for methods/functions; use appropriate PHP type hints. Prefer PHPDoc blocks over inli
